findings.title: Acceptance gives the means an integrity condition
findings.claim: The means of approach in 5:35 is pursued through guarded integrity: the earlier offering scene makes reception, rather than presentation alone, decisive.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers at 5:35:6:2 and 5:35:4:1 meet the 5:27 sequence of drawing near, offering, repeated acceptance, and acceptance from the protected. That contact changes the prior reading of the means as a technique that itself secures nearness into an approach whose reception depends on the seeker's guarded condition.
findings.reader_payoff: Approach becomes a relation that joins seeking with the condition of the seeker, so the reader can perceive why taqwa stands before the search for a means.
findings.containment: The finding does not generalize one offering scene into a rule that every means or offering is accepted. The supplied context morphology is lean and the qrb and qbl branch identities are unresolved; those parts remain HFT-attributed, while the live alternative is that 5:27 describes one failed ritual approach without defining wasila generally.

epistemic.reason: All anchors and HFT roles are supplied, but the support marks the Arabic as surface evidence only, target morphology is absent, and two context branches have no independent lexicon descriptor.

findings.title: Direction and effect diagnose striving
findings.claim: Striving in His path is read as effort whose moral identity comes from its direction and life-ordering effect, while the surrounding violent movement supplies a counterimage.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers at 5:35:9:2 and 5:35:11:1 meet the 5:28 contrast between extending and withholding a hand, the 5:32 balance between killing and preserving life, and the 5:33 coupling of hostile movement with corruption. This changes the prior reading of jihad as identifiable by force or hardship alone into effort diagnosed by its route and consequence.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why the focus binds exertion to His path: intensity alone does not explain the difference between life-preserving direction and motion toward corruption.
findings.containment: The hostile and punitive material in 5:33 remains a live contextual pressure, and the finding is a directional boundary rather than an absolute claim about nonviolence. The 5:32 connection includes reciprocal counterevidence and is retained rather than filtered.

epistemic.reason: The HFT trace supplies exact pericope coordinates and roles, but the context morphology is absent and the context branch identities remain unresolved and attributed.

findings.title: The means leaves a route of return
findings.claim: The means of approach can include a timely return for someone still implicated in wrongdoing: before capture closes voluntary agency, repentance, forgiveness, and mercy can reorient a damaged path toward God.

That contact changes the prior reading of the means as a route only for people already moving cleanly forward into a contextual possibility of return while agency remains open.
findings.reader_payoff: The command to seek a means can be heard as addressing a person who needs reorientation, not only a person who already stands outside the damage described before the focus.
findings.containment: This is one contextual shape of the means, not a replacement for the plain command or a general definition of 5:34. The live alternative is that 5:34 states only the legal status of the preceding offenders. All unresolved branch material remains attributed.

epistemic.reason: The exact 5:34 and 5:35 coordinates and HFT roles are supplied, while the context morphology and five of the branch descriptors are not independently supplied.

That contact changes the prior reading of the means as a valuable resource saved for a favorable outcome into passage-work performed while seeking, protection, and exertion remain possible.
findings.reader_payoff: The temporal force of the focus becomes visible: the route is something one travels and enacts, while a later equivalent cannot purchase passage.
findings.containment: The finding uses the immediately following verses as a contrast and does not claim that every later passage classifies wasila. The live alternative is that 5:36–37 describe eschatological impossibility without defining the means. The unresolved fdy, qbl, and kh rj branches remain attributed.
